resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy (sale or rental)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Union Beach Office of Code Enforcement (Code Enforcement Officer)
resale_co.lead_time: Inspections are held every half hour: Monday, Tuesday and Thursday 9:30am to 3pm, Wednesday 9:30am to 11am. Bring the application with a preferred day and time in mind.
requirements: Code Enforcement inspection for compliance with the International Property Maintenance Code (2015 edition) as adopted by the Borough
Smoke detectors in working order sufficient to warn all occupants, plus one in the basement or cellar, before the CO is issued (Borough Code 10-3)
If the house has not been raised, a Zoning-Floodplain Development application must be completed before the CO can be issued
Application lists the prospective owner or tenant and everyone who will occupy the home
Fees paid by check or money order only

fees.label: Certificate of Occupancy, commercial or multi-family dwelling (likely includes a 2 family home)
Third inspection and each later reinspection, single family residence
fees.quote: If a third inspection is required because the applicant failed to correct all of the violations, deficiencies or other noncompliances an additional fee of $50 shall be charged prior to the issuance of the certificate of occupancy.

fees.label: Third inspection and each later reinspection, commercial or multi-family
fees.quote: If a third inspection is required because the applicant failed to correct all of the violations, deficiencies or other noncompliances an additional fee of $100 shall be charged prior to the issuance of the certificate of occupancy.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Certificate of Occupancy application from the Code Enforcement forms page, mark it for a sale, and drop it off at Code Enforcement, Municipal Building, 650 Poole Avenue, Union Beach, NJ 07735, with a check or money order. Pick an inspection day and time when you drop it off. The fee covers the first inspection and one reinspection.

evidence.quote: A Certificate of Occupancy is required for all rentals or sales of properties.
Payable by check or money order only
Office Hours: 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM Monday thru Friday
IF THE HOUSE HAS NOT BEEN RAISED, A FLOODPLAIN APPLICATION HAS TO BE COMPLETED BEFORE A C.O. CAN BE ISSUED.

For a single family residence a fee of $100 to cover the cost of the application and of the first inspection and any reinspection to confirm the correction of violations, deficiencies or other noncompliances prior to the issuance of the certificate of occupancy.

Effective immediately no certificate of occupancy shall be issued for any dwelling or dwelling unit after it has become vacant unless such dwelling or dwelling unit has installed smoke detectors sufficient in number to warn all occupants of the dwelling.

resale_co.notes: The Code Enforcement page says a CO is required for all sales and rentals. Borough Code 10-2.4 (Ord. No. 2016-229, read through the ecode360 print view) sets the same $100 and $125 fees and makes the code official responsible. The Code Enforcement page shows CodeEnforcement@unionbeachnj.gov as the email, but the mailto link behind it points to CodeEnforcer@unionbeachnj.gov; the officer's own address is abencosme@unionbeachnj.gov. The CO checklist PDF linked on the page returned 403 Forbidden and could not be read. Tenant/Landlord registration is required at the time of a CO when ownership or occupancy changes for rental units only; it is not a resale requirement for an owner-occupied home. The Borough's fire code (Code 9-2.7) also lists an R-A fee of $20 for non-owner occupied 1 and 2 unit homes, charged only upon sale or change of tenant; that is a rental registration item, not the smoke certificate fee.

requirements: Smoke and carbon monoxide alarm certificate required before a 1 or 2 family home is sold (N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3)

No Borough checklist for the certificate was found online; state rules apply (smoke alarm on each level and outside sleeping areas, 10-year sealed battery units where battery-only, CO alarm near sleeping areas when there is a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage)

authorities.name: Union Beach Fire Department, Bureau of Fire Prevention (Fire Marshal)
authorities.how_to_apply: No online application or fee schedule was found. Contact the Fire Marshal (firemarshal@unionbeachnj.gov) or the Borough at 732-264-2277 to request the smoke and CO certificate inspection.

evidence.quote: The local enforcing agency shall be the "Union Beach Fire Department" through its bureau of fire prevention, which is hereby created herein.

LEAID: 1350-001 Union Beach Boro SMOKE DETECTOR COMPLIANCE Name: Union Beach Boro Bldg Dept Enf Auth. Fire Dept Addr: 650 Poole Av Fire Official Elizabeth Sweeney Phone (732) 264-2277 Email firemarshal@unionbeachnj.gov

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA fire directory lists the Fire Department as the enforcing agency, but names "Union Beach Boro Bldg Dept" at 650 Poole Avenue (the Municipal Building) as the smoke detector compliance office, so the request may go through Borough Hall. No smoke certificate fee was found in the Borough code or on the Borough site, so no fee is listed. Search results that seemed to show Union Beach fees were from other towns' codes and were not used.

other_items.label: Floodplain application for homes not raised
other_items.detail: If the house has not been raised, a Zoning-Floodplain Development application must be completed before the Certificate of Occupancy can be issued.

open_questions: Who does the smoke and CO certificate inspection for a sale (Fire Marshal or Borough Hall), what are the fees, and how far ahead must it be requested?
Is a 2 family home charged the $100 single-family fee or the $125 multi-family fee?
How long is the Certificate of Occupancy valid, and what is on the CO checklist (the PDF could not be opened)?
